title: Definition
body_md: We say $f$ is partially $\mathcal{C}^2$ if the map $y \rightarrow$ $D_\mu f(\mu)(y)$ is continuously differentiable with a derivative $(\mu, y) \rightarrow \partial_y D_\mu f(\mu)(y)$ jointly continuous on $\mathcal{P}_2\left(\mathbb{R}\right) \times \mathbb{R}$.
head: environment

label: lem:ito
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:ito}
	Consider following process
	$$
d X_t=b_t d t+\sigma_t d B_t+ d K_t\,,
$$
where $K_t$ is a deterministic, 
continuous and nondecreasing process with $K_0 = 0$, 
$\left(b_t\right)_{t\geq0}$ and $\left(\sigma_t\right)_{t\geq 0}$ are progressively measurable with values in $\mathbb{R}$ and satisfy following integrable condition:
$$
\mathbb{E}\left[\int_0^T\left(\left|b_s\right|^2+\left|\sigma_s\right|^4\right) d s\right]<+\infty\,.
$$
If $f$ is partially $\mathcal{C}^2$, we have 
$$
\begin{gathered}
f\left(\mathcal{L}_{X_t}\right)=f\left(\mathcal{L}_{X_0}\right)+\int_0^t \mathbb{E}\left[D_\mu f\left(\mathcal{L}_{X_t}\right)\left(X_s\right)b_s\right] d s+\int_0^t \mathbb{E}\left[D_\mu f\left(\mathcal{L}_{X_t}\right)\left(X_s\right)\right] d K_s \\
+\frac{1}{2} \int_0^t \mathbb{E}\left[\left(\sigma_s^2\partial_y D_\mu f\left(\mathcal{L}_{X_t}\right)\left(X_s\right)\right)\right] d s.
\end{gathered}
$$

label: ass:A_1
title: Assumption
body_md:
\label{ass:A_1}
\begin{enumerate}[(i)]
	\item Lipschitz assumption: there exists a constant $K>0$ such that for all $x,y \in \mathbb{R}$, $\mu,\nu \in \mathcal{P}_2(\mathbb{R})$ we have 
	$$
	|b(x,\mu) - b(y,\nu)| + |\sigma(x,\mu)- \sigma(y,\nu)|\leq K\left( |x - y| + \mathcal{W}_2(\mu,\nu) \right)\,.
	$$
	\item The random variable $\xi$ is square integrable, i.e. $\mathbb{E}\left[ \xi^2 \right]<\infty$ and satisfies $\mathbb{E}\left[ h(\xi) \right]\geq 0$.
\end{enumerate}

label: pro:3.2
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{pro:3.2}
Suppose that Assumptions \ref{ass:A_1} and \ref{ass:A_2} hold.  
\begin{enumerate}[(i)]
	\item  For all $p$, there exists a positive $C_p$, depending on $T, b, \sigma$ and $h$ such that 
$$
\mathbb{E}\left[ \sup_{t\leq T}|X_t|^p \right] \leq C_p(1+\mathbb{E}\left[ |\xi|^p \right])\,.
$$

	\item There exists a positive constant $C$, depending on $T, b, \sigma$ and $h$ such that 
$$
\forall 0\leq s\leq t\leq T ,\quad |K_t-K_s| \leq C|t-s|^{\frac{1}{2}}\,.
$$
	\item For all $p\geq 1$ such that $\xi \in L^p$ we have 
$$
\forall 0\leq s\leq t\leq T ,\quad \mathbb{E}\left[ \left|X_t-X_s\right|^p \right]\leq C|t-s|^{\frac{p}{2}}\,.
$$
\end{enumerate}

For given $X_0\in \mathbb{R}$ and $t_0\geq 0$, let us set $\mu_s : = \mathcal{L}_{X_s^{t_0,X_0}}$. Then, by Lemma \ref{lem:ito}, 
	$$
	u(T,\mu_T) = u(t_0,\mu_{t_0}) + \int_{t_0}^T\left( \partial_t + \mathcal{T} \right)u(s,\mu_s) + \int_{t_0}^T\int_\mathbb{R}D_\mu u(s,\mu_s)(y) \mu_s(dy) dK_s 	\,,
 $$
	where, by \eqref{eq:FK_f}-(ii), 
	$$
	\int_{t_0}^T\int_{\mathbb{R}}D_\mu u(s,\mu_s)(y) \mu_s(dy)dK_s = \int_{t_0}^T\mathbbm{1}_{\left \{ \mu_s \in \partial \mathcal{O} \right \}} \left( \int_{\mathbb{R}}D_\mu u(s,\mu_s) (y)  \right)dK_s = 0\,.
	$$
	From the equation satisfied by $u$, we obtain
	$$
	u(t_0,\mu_0) = u(t_0,\mu_{t_0}) = \mathbb{E}\left[ u(T,\mu_T) \right] = \mathbb{E}\left[ G(\mathcal{L}_{X_T}) \right]\,.

title: Remark
body_md:
Unlike in \cite{briand2020particles} [Theorem 3.3], improving the regularity of $h$ does not improve the convergence speed of propagation of chaos. This is because in this case, the drift coefficient and diffusion coefficient are both related to the law of the solution. We need to control $$
|b(\bar{X}^i_t,\mathcal{L}_{\bar{X}^i_s}) - b({X}^i_t,\frac{1}{n}\sum_{j=1}^n \delta_{X^j_s})|^2+|\sigma(\bar{X}^i_t,\mathcal{L}_{\bar{X}^i_s}) - \sigma({X}^i_t,\frac{1}{n}\sum_{j=1}^n \delta_{X^j_s})|^2
$$ and the convergence speed of this part is $n^{-\frac{1}{2}}$.

label: thm:LDP

head: environment
name: Large deviation principle

title: Proof
body_md:
According to Proposition \ref{pro:5.1} , there exists a measurable map $\mathcal{G}^0$: 
	$$
	\mathcal{G}^0 : C\left([0, T] ; \mathbb{R}\right) \rightarrow \mathcal{X} \,,
	$$
	such that for any $h \in L^2([0,T],\mathbb{R})$
	$$
	Y^h = \mathcal{G}^0\left( \int_0^\cdot h(s)ds \right).
	$$
	Let $$
\mathcal{H}^M:=\left\{h:[0, T] \rightarrow \mathbb{R}^m, \int_0^T\|h(s)\|^2 \mathrm{~d} s \leq M\right\}\,,
$$
and
$$\tilde{\mathcal{H}}^M:=\left\{h: h\right. \text{is }\mathbb{R}\text{-valued }\mathcal{F}_t\text{-predictable process such that } h(\omega) \in \mathcal{H}^M, \mathbb{P}-a.s \}\,.$$

$\mathcal{H}^M$ is endowed with the weak topology on $L^2\left([0, T], \mathbb{R}\right)$. Then $\mathcal{H}^M$ is a Polish space. For every $\varepsilon > 0$, there exists a measurable mapping $\mathcal{G}^\varepsilon(\cdot) :C\left([0, T] ; \mathbb{R}\right) \rightarrow \mathcal{X} $ such that 
$$
X^\varepsilon = \mathcal{G}^\varepsilon(B(\cdot))\,,
$$
and for any $M > 0$ and $h^\varepsilon \in \tilde{\mathcal{H}}^M$ , 
$$
Z^{\varepsilon}:=\mathcal{G}^{\varepsilon}\left(B(\cdot)+\frac{1}{\sqrt{\varepsilon}} \int_0^{\cdot} h^{\varepsilon}(s) \mathrm{d} s\right)\,.
$$
From  Girsanov's Theorem, we know $Z^\varepsilon$  is the solution of the following MR-MVSDE:
\begin{equation}\label{eq:Z}
\begin{aligned}
	  \left\{\begin{array}{l}
	  Z^\varepsilon_t = \xi + \int_0^t b\left( Z^\varepsilon_s,\mathcal{L}_{X^\varepsilon_s} \right)ds + \int_0^t \sigma\left( Y^h_s,\mathcal{L}_{X^\varepsilon_s} \right)h^\varepsilon(s)ds + K^{Z^\varepsilon}_t\\
	  \mathbb{E}\left[ h(Z^\varepsilon_t) \right]\geq 0, \quad \int_0^t h(Z^\varepsilon_s)dK^{Z^\varepsilon}_s = 0
	  \end{array}\right. \,.
\end{aligned}
\end{equation}
Following \cite{liu2022large}, we only need to verify the two claims:
\begin{itemize}
	\item [\textbf{(LDP1)}]  For every $M<+\infty$ and any family $\left\{h^n ; n \in \mathbb{N}\right\} \subset \mathcal{H}^M$ converging to some element $h \in \mathcal{H}^M$ as $n \rightarrow \infty$
	$$
	\lim\limits_{n\rightarrow \infty} \sup_{t\in [0,T]}\left|\mathcal{G}^0\left( \int_0^{\cdot}h^n(s)ds \right) - \mathcal{G}^0\left( \int_0^{\cdot}h(s)ds \right)\right| = 0\,.
	$$
	\item [\textbf{(LDP2)}] For every $M<+\infty$ and any family $\left\{h^{\varepsilon} ; \varepsilon>0\right\} \subset \tilde{\mathcal{H}}^M$ and any $\theta>0$,
$$
	\lim_{\varepsilon\rightarrow 0}\mathbb{P}\left[ \sup_{t\in [0,T]}\left|Z^\varepsilon_t - Y^{h^\varepsilon}_t\right| \geq \theta \right] = 0\,,
	$$
where $Z^{\varepsilon}$ is the unique solution to \eqref{eq:Z} and $Y^{h^{\varepsilon}}=\mathcal{G}^0\left(\int_0^\cdot h^{\varepsilon}(s) \mathrm{d} s\right)$.
\end{itemize}

The verification of (LDP1) will be given in Proposition \ref{pro:LDP1}. (LDP2) will be established in Proposition \ref{pro:LDP2}.

body_md:
\label{lem:6.1}
	Suppose Assumptions \ref{ass:A_1}, \ref{ass:A_2} and \ref{ass:A_5} hold, let $X_t$ and $Y_t$ be two solution of \eqref{eq:1.1} such that $\mathcal{L}_{\xi^{X_0}} = \mu_0$, $\mathcal{L}_{\xi^{Y_0}} = \nu_0$ and $\mathcal{W}_2\left( \mu_0,\nu_0 \right)^2 = \mathbb{E}\left[ \left|\xi^{X_0}-\xi^{Y_0}\right|^2 \right]$. We have 
	$$
	\mathcal{W}_2\left( P^*_{t}\mu_0,P^*_t\nu_0 \right)^2\leq \mathrm{e}^{-\left(C_2-C_1\right) t} \mathcal{W}_2\left(\mu_0, \nu_0\right)^2\,.

head: environment
name: Exponential convergence

label: eq:lem_6_1_1
title: Proof
body_md:
From the definition of $P^*_t$, we have $P^*_t\mu_0 = \mu_t$, $P^*_t\nu_0 = \nu_t$. 
	
	Apply It\^{o}'s lemma to $(X_t- Y_t)^2$, we have 
	\begin{equation}\label{eq:lem_6_1_1}
\begin{aligned}
	  \left( X_t - Y_t \right)^2 &= (\xi^{X_0}-\xi^{Y_0})^2+\int_0^t 2\left( X_t - Y_t \right)\left[ b(X_t,\mu_t) - b(Y_t,\nu_t) \right]dt + \int_0^t \sigma(X_t,\mu_t) - \sigma(Y_t,\nu_t)dt \\
	  &\qquad+ \int_0^t 2\left( X_t - Y_t \right)\left[ \sigma(X_t,\mu_t) - \sigma(Y_t,\nu_t) \right]dB_t + \int_0^t 2(X_t-Y_t)d(K^X_t - K^Y_t)\,.
	  \end{aligned}
\end{equation}
Since $X_t$ and $Y_t$ is the solution of \eqref{eq:1.1} and $h$ is bi-Lipschitz , we have $\mathbb{E}\left[ X_t \right]\geq 0$ and $\mathbb{E}\left[ Y_t \right]\geq 0$. Combining  $K^X_t$ and $K^Y_t$ are non-decrease processes,  we have 
$$
\int_0^t\mathbb{E}\left[ X_t \right]dK^Y_t\geq 0\,, \quad \int_0^t\mathbb{E}\left[ Y_t \right]dK^X_t \geq 0\,.
$$
By the definition of solution \eqref{eq:1.1}, we obtain $$
\int_0^t\mathbb{E}\left[ h(X_t) \right]dK^X_t =\int_0^t \mathbb{E}\left[ h(Y_t) \right]dK^Y_t = 0\,.
$$
Taking expectation of \eqref{eq:lem_6_1_1} and applying stochastic Fubini's Theorem, we have the following estimation 
$$
\mathbb{E}\left( X_t - Y_t \right)^2\leq  (\xi^{X_0}-\xi^{Y_0})^2+\mathbb{E}\int_0^t 2\left( X_t - Y_t \right)\left[ b(X_t,\mu_t) - b(Y_t,\nu_t) \right]dt + \mathbb{E}\int_0^t \sigma(X_t,\mu_t) - \sigma(Y_t,\nu_t)dt $$
Apply Assumption \ref{ass:A_5}  and Gronwall's lemma, we obtain
$$
\mathcal{W}_2\left( P^*_{t}\mu_0,P^*_t\nu_0 \right)^2 \leq \mathbb{E}\left[ |X_t-Y_t|^2 \right]\leq e^{-(C_2-C_1)t}\mathbb{E}\left[ |\xi^{X_0}-\xi^{Y_0}|^2 \right]\leq  e^{-(C_2-C_1)t} \mathcal{W}_2\left(\mu_0, \nu_0\right)^2\,.
$$

label: thm:eipm
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:eipm}
Suppose Assumptions \ref{ass:A_1}, \ref{ass:A_2} and \ref{ass:A_5} hold. $P_t$ has a unique invariant probability measure $\mu \in \mathcal{P}_2$ i.e. $P_t^* \mu=\mu, t>0$ such that 
$$
\mathcal{W}_2\left(P_t^* \nu_0, \mu\right)^2 \leq \mathcal{W}_2\left(\nu_0, \mu\right)^2 \mathrm{e}^{-\left(C_2-C_1\right) t}, \quad t \geq 0, \nu_0 \in \mathcal{P}_2 .
$$

name: Existence of invariant probability measure

label: eq:thm_6_2_1
title: Proof
body_md:
{We first show that there exists a $\mu \in \mathcal{P}_2(\mathbb{R})$} such that 
	\begin{equation}\label{eq:thm_6_2_1}
\begin{aligned}
	  	\lim_{t\rightarrow \infty}\mathcal{W}_2\left( P^*_t\delta_0,\mu \right) = 0\,.
\end{aligned}
\end{equation}
	To this end, it suffices to show that $\left\{P_t^* \delta_0\right\}_{t \geq 0}$ is a $\mathcal{W}_{2}$-Cauchy family when $t \rightarrow \infty$. Using the semigroup property of  $P_{t+s}^*$ and the exponential convergence, we have
$$
\begin{aligned}
 \mathcal{W}_2\left(P_{t+s}^* \delta_0, P_t^* \delta_0\right)^2 \leq \mathcal{W}_2\left(P_s^* \delta_0, \delta_0\right)^2 \mathrm{e}^{-\left(C_2-C_1\right) t}  =\mathrm{e}^{-\left(C_2-C_1\right) t} \mathbb{E}\left|X_s^0\right|^2, \quad s, t \geq 0 \,,
\end{aligned}
$$
where $X^0_s$ is a solution of MR-MVSDE whose initial condition is $\xi = 0$. Then, we only need to show 
$$
\sup_{s\geq 0}\mathbb{E}\left[ |X^0_s|^2 \right]< \infty\,.
$$
It is true from Proposition \ref{pro:3.2}. By \eqref{eq:thm_6_2_1}, $P^*_{t+s} = P^*_t P^*_s$ and 
$$
\mathcal{W}_2\left( P^*_t\mu_1,P^*_t \mu_2 \right)\leq e^{-(C_2-C_1)t/2}\mathcal{W}_2\left( \mu_1,\mu_2 \right)\,,
$$
we obtain that
$$
\mathcal{W}_2\left( P^*_t\mu,\mu \right) = \lim_{s\rightarrow \infty}\mathcal{W}_2\left( P^*_t \mu , P^*_{t+s}\delta_0 \right)\leq e^{-(C_2-C_1)t/2}\lim_{s\rightarrow \infty}\mathcal{W}_2\left( \mu,P^*_s\delta_0 \right) = 0\,.
$$
That means $P^*_t \mu = \mu$.

body_md:
\label{thm:lhi}
Suppose Assumptions \ref{ass:A_1} and \ref{ass:A_2} hold and $\sigma(x)^{-1}<\infty$. Let $0\leq s<t\leq T$
\begin{enumerate}[(i)]
	\item For any $\mu_0,\nu_0\in \mathcal{P}_2(\mathbb{R})$,
	$$
	\left(P_{s, t} \log f\right)\left(\nu_0\right) \leq \log \left(P_{s, t} f\right)\left(\mu_0\right)+\phi(s, t) \mathcal{W}_2\left(\mu_0, \nu_0\right)^2\,, \quad f \in \mathcal{B}_b^{+}\left(\mathbb{R}\right)\,.
	$$
	Consequently,
	$$
\left|\nabla P_{s, t} f\right|^2 \leq 2 \phi(s, t)\left\{P_{s, t} f^2-\left(P_{s, t} f\right)^2\right\}, \quad f \in \mathcal{B}_b\left(\mathbb{R}\right)\,.
$$
	\item For any different $\mu_0,\nu_0\in \mathcal{P}_2(\mathbb{R})$ and $f \in \mathcal{B}_b^{+}\left(\mathbb{R}\right)$,
	$$
	\begin{aligned}
& \frac{\left|\left(P_{s, t} f\right)\left(\mu_0\right)-\left(P_{s, t} f\right)\left(\nu_0\right)\right|^2}{\mathcal{W}_2\left(\mu_0, \nu_0\right)^2}  \quad \leq 2 \phi(s, t) \sup _{\nu \in B\left(\mu_0, \mathcal{W}_2\left(\mu_0, \nu_0\right)\right)}\left\{\left(P_{s, t} f^2\right)(\nu)-\left(P_{s, t} f\right)^2(\nu)\right\} \,,
\end{aligned}
	$$
 where $B(\mu_0, \mathcal{W}_2(\mu_0, \nu_0))$ is a ball in the Wasserstein spaces $\mathcal{P}_2(\mathbb{R})$ with radius  $\mathcal{W}_2(\mu_0, \nu_0)$.
		Consequently,
		$$
		\begin{aligned}
\left\|P_{s, t}^* \mu_0-P_{s, t}^* v_0\right\|_{v a r} & :=2 \sup _{A \in \mathcal{B}_b\left(\mathbb{R}\right)}\left|\left(P_{s, t}^* \mu_0\right)(A)-\left(P_{s, t}^* v_0\right)(A)\right| \leq \sqrt{2 \phi(s, t)} \mathcal{W}_2\left(\mu_0, v_0\right) .
\end{aligned}
		$$
\end{enumerate}

label: thm:shi
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:shi}
 Suppose Assumptions \ref{ass:A_1} and \ref{ass:A_2} hold and $\sigma(\mu)$ is invertible with $\sigma(\mu) + \sigma(\mu)^{-1} $ is bounded.
For any $p>1$, $t\in [0,T]$, $\mu \in \mathcal{P}_2(\mathbb{R})$, $\nu \in \mathcal{P}_2(\mathbb{R})$ and $f\in \mathcal{B}^+_b(\mathbb{R})$, we have 
 	$$
 	\left( P_t f \right)^p(\mu_0)\leq \left( P_t f(v + \cdot)^p \right)(\mu_0)\exp{\frac{p\int_0^t \sigma(\mu_s)^{-2}\left \{ |v|/t + s|v|/t \right \}^2ds}{2(p-1)}}\,.
 	$$
 	Moreover, for any $f\in \mathcal{B}_b^+(\mathbb{R})$ with $f>1$,
 	$$
 	\left( P_t \log f \right)(\mu_0)\leq \log\left( P_t f (v + \cdot) \right)(\mu_0) + \frac{1}{2}\int_0^t\sigma(\mu_s)^{-2} \left \{ |v|/t + s|v|/t \right \}^2ds\,.
 	$$

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $Y_t = X_t + \frac{tv}{T}$, then 
	$$
	dY_t = b(Y_t,\mu_t)dt + \sigma(\mu_t)d\tilde{B}_t + dK_t\,,
	$$ 
	where 
	$$
	\begin{aligned}
		\tilde{B}_t &: = B_t + \int_0^t \eta_s ds\,,\\
		\eta_t &: = \sigma(\mu_t)^{-1}\left \{ \frac{v}{T}+ b(X_t,\mu_t) - b(X_t + \frac{t v}{T},\mu_t) \right \}.
	\end{aligned}
	$$
	Let $R_T = \exp\left \{ \int_0^T \eta_s dW_s - \frac{1}{2}\int_0^T |\eta_s|^2ds \right \}$. Since $\mathbb{E}\left[ \exp(\frac{1}{2}\int_0^T |\eta_s|^2ds) \right]< \infty$, from Nokikov's condition, we deduce that $R_t$ is a martingale and $\mathbb{E} R_T = 1$. By the Girsanov's Theorem, we can get
	$$
	\left( P_Tf \right)(\mu_0) = \mathbb{E}\left[ R_T f(Y_T) \right] = \mathbb{E}\left[ R_Tf(X_T + v) \right]\leq \left( P_T f(v+\cdot)^p \right)^{\frac{1}{p}}(\mu_0) \left( \mathbb{E} R_T^{\frac{p}{p-1}} \right)^{\frac{p-1}{p}}\,.
	$$
	Applying Young's inequality, we obtain 
	$$
	\begin{aligned}
			\left( P_T\log f \right)(\mu_0) &= \mathbb{E}\left[ R_T \log f(Y_T) \right] = \mathbb{E}\left[ R_T\log f\left( X_T + v \right) \right]\\
			&\leq \log P_T f(v + \cdot)(\mu_0) + \mathbb{E}\left[ R_T\log R_T \right]\,.
	\end{aligned}
	$$
	Then we have 
$$
	  \mathbb{E} R_T^{\frac{p}{p-1}}\leq \exp\left \{ \frac{p}{2(p-1)^2}\int_0^T |\eta_s|^2ds \right \}\leq \exp\left \{ \frac{p \int_0^T \sigma(\mu_t)^{-2}\left \{ |v|/T + t|v|/T \right \}^2dt}{2(p-1)^2} \right \}\,,
$$
and 
$$
\mathbb{E} \left[  R_T \log R_T \right] = \mathbb{E}^{\mathbb{Q}}\log R_T \leq \frac{1}{2}  \mathbb{E}^{\mathbb{Q}} \int_0^T|\eta_s|^2ds \leq \frac{1}{2}\int_0^T \sigma(\mu_t)^{-2}\left \{ |v|/T + t|v|/T \right \}^2dt\,.
$$
